findings.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers
findings.triageReason: Intended design (confirmed by protocol owner). The underwater buffer pays daily-volume withdrawals at par during transient, mean-reverting underwater dips to avoid sparking panic and to avoid forcing users to realise losses by redeeming shares at the bottom; bank-run / mass-exit is handled separately by migrateOut with pro-rata distribution. The report itself concedes there is no incremental victim (the slow staker is baseline-unchanged vs a no-buffer world). The buffer-at-par path implements the documented invariant 'a non-migrating user cannot be forced to realise a loss', and both of the finding's recommended fixes (block the buffer branch / pro-rata haircut) would defeat that design goal. Reclassified from Medium to intended-design via /review-finding.
findings.coverageNote: stable-staker-07: this wont-fix is buffer-scoped on _routeExit. Finding M-05 (0dca43f3) is the strictly-larger BUFFERLESS exposure keyed on emergencyWithdraw and explicitly does NOT inherit this wont-fix (distinct fingerprint, incremental inter-user victim, not blessed by known issue #6). findings.title: Terminal migration has no mint-free escape hatch if phUSD minter rights are revoked mid-migration
findings.description: During an active terminal migration, emergencyWithdraw is blocked (migration active), and the only exits (userMigrate, batchMigrate) mint frozen pending phUSD via _exitPosition -> phUSD.mint BEFORE transferring principal. If the staker loses phUSD minter rights while a token is active, those exits revert on the pending-phUSD mint and principal is retrievable only after minter rights are restored. Healthy mode has a mint-free escape (emergencyWithdraw); terminal mode does not. Bounded by the owner-trusted precondition 'minter revoked mid-migration'.
findings.impact: Owner-trust-bounded availability: principal is not permanently lost, but is temporarily unrecoverable from terminal-migration exits until phUSD minter rights are restored.
findings.reconfirmedThisRun: stable-staker-07 (CLASS-003 / M-03): re-confirmed live at HEAD 7e9ef80; userMigrate relocated to L495-504 (was L478-503). Carryover stub emitted.

Held at Medium not High (principal recoverable once minter restored). Authoritative severity remains LOW until human triage.

findings.title: Idle-pool strategy adoption discards creditedPrincipal, shorting last withdrawers
findings.description: The story-005 fix made stake/depositFor/_routeDeposit credit IYieldStrategy.deposit's returned creditedPrincipal, but the setYieldStrategy adoption sweep strategy.deposit(token, idleBalance, address(this)) discards the return (L215). Adopting a haircutting (market) strategy over a non-empty idle pool leaves poolInfo.totalStaked at full nominal value while strategy.principalOf(this) = idleBalance * (1 - slip), producing a silent last-withdrawer FCFS shortfall on the healthy-withdraw path; the underwater guard is blind because it compares strategy-internal totalBalanceOf vs principalOf. The gap becomes skimmable protocol surplus unrecoverable by users.

findings.title: depositFor missing require(credited > 0) guard

findings.title: setYieldStrategy lacks !active guard — sweeps the realized payout pile R into a strategy, bricks the userMigrate escape hatch and strands migrants' principal
findings.description: After initiateMigration decouples the strategy and parks R as idle balance, calling setYieldStrategy on the migrating token re-approves a strategy and sweeps R back into it (L213-216) because there is no require(!migrationInfo[token].active) guard. batchMigrate/userMigrate then safeTransfer from the now-empty idle pile and revert, so every migrant's principal is stranded inside the new strategy with no in-contract recovery path. Distinct from M-01/dab5a656 on the same function via rootCauseClass. NOT covered by known issue #7 (HEALTHY-pool rewire).
findings.impact: Escape-hatch availability destroyed plus permanent principal stranding during an active terminal migration. Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun.

findings.title: Underwater buffer-path withdraw desyncs totalStaked < strategy.principalOf, making initiateMigration's L392 post-check unsatisfiable — terminal migration permanently un-initiable
findings.description: A story-002 underwater buffer-path withdraw decrements pool.totalStaked without touching strategy principal, leaving strategy.principalOf > totalStaked. initiateMigration requests _routeExit(token, P=totalStaked) (L387) which under-drains the strategy, so the L392-395 require(principalOf == 0) reverts on every attempt and the token can never enter terminal migration.
findings.impact: No principal loss; permanent loss of the terminal-migration/upgrade-escape FEATURE for the affected token (function/availability). Distinct upstream cause and code location from acknowledged 3d61c955 (migrateOut) — kept separate to avoid burying a live liveness defect (Law 1).
findings.relatedLedger: 3d61c955 (acknowledged, recheck LIKELY-FIXED) — shared SYMPTOM only, NOT merged.

findings.title: emergencyWithdraw realizes underwater loss FCFS via direct share over-redemption (bufferless par bank-run): early exiters whole, late exiters absorb the entire shortfall
findings.description: emergencyWithdraw passes guardUnderwater=false (L316), so _routeExit redeems requested principal from the strategy at the depressed price. First callers receive full principal (over-redeeming shares), draining the position; late callers receive less than principal or revert, absorbing the entire pre-existing strategy shortfall. Inter-user value socialization gated on an external underwater market condition.
findings.impact: Value leak (inter-user loss socialization): late stakers lose principal to early stakers. Total payout never exceeds strategy realizable value (no protocol theft); already-incurred loss is mis-distributed FCFS rather than pro-rata.
findings.wontFixCoverage: Keyed on emergencyWithdraw (fingerprint 0dca43f3), NOT _routeExit. Does NOT inherit/collide with wont-fix 69c7666 (src/StableStaker.sol:_routeExit:fcfs-loss-socialization) — strictly-larger BUFFERLESS exposure with an incremental inter-user victim; not blessed by known issue #6. findings.title: Migration credit asymmetry: operator batchMigrate books users below principal through a haircutting destination strategy while userMigrate keeps full value
findings.description: Batch-migrated users are booked below their old-staker principal: StableStakerMigrator.migrate (L76-80) redeposits each credit via newStaker.depositFor -> _routeDeposit, which a haircutting destination strategy reduces to credited = amount*(1-slip). A user who instead self-exits via userMigrate receives tokens at full credit. Equal-principal users diverge purely by exit method, breaking the migrator's principal-preservation/equivalence story. Magnitude = destination slippageToleranceBps; zero when the destination is idle/full-credit at migration time.
findings.impact: Law-2 faithfulness gap (deposit-side principal-preservation break). Honest severity Low (bounded by destination slip, config-dependent). Non-obvious owner footgun.

findings.title: phUSDPerDay sub-86400-wei/day budget floors phusdPerSecond to 0 (silent zero emission)
findings.description: Owner sets amountPerDay < SECONDS_PER_DAY (86400 base units) -> perSecond = amountPerDay/86400 = 0 (L169) -> the pool silently emits ZERO rewards with no revert; stakers accrue nothing while believing a budget is live. Distinct from the accepted integer-division DUST class (known issue #2 / wont-fix 35e9be8d), which rounds DOWN but does not bless a complete zero-emission state. Only the sub-86400 silent-zero edge is classified here.
findings.impact: QA non-obvious owner-config footgun; no value at risk for realistic 18-decimal phUSD budgets. Recommend require(perSecond > 0) or input scaling.
